catalog_quote: Breeze found that stress was not contrastive in Dizin or Benchnon "but generally falls on the first syllable of a word" (1988:482). This needs to be researched further.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: confirmed verbatim in the held Beachy 2005 PDF at printed p.47, section 2.6. (2) The classification 'fixed-strict initial, dom=true' rests on a single second-hand sentence: Beachy 2005 (MA thesis) quoting Breeze 1988:482 that stress is non-contrastive and 'generally' initial, immediately followed by Beachy's own 'This needs to be researched further'; Dizin is analysed by all sources as a three-level tone language, and Beachy p.56 again flags stress as uninvestigated. Nothing found contradicts initial stress, but 'generally' plus the explicit hedge makes 'strict' stronger than the source; the evidence is thin rather than wrong. (3) Better/primary sources exist but are not held: Breeze 1988 itself (print only), Seyoum 2021 phonology article (RG author upload, blocked from our machine

sources.quote: Beachy 2005:47 (section 2.6 Stress, quoting Breeze 1988:482): "Breeze found that stress was not contrastive in Dizin or Benchnon \"but generally falls on the first syllable of a word\" (1988:482). This needs to be researched further." Also relevant, Beachy 2005:47 (section 2.7 Tone): "Keefer (1969b:2), Allen (1978:379), Breeze (1988:481), and Aklilu (2003:67) all analyzed Dizin as having three phonemic tone levels: low, mid, and high."
